title: Stability-Aware Feature Design for Robust Watermark Detection in Machine-Generated Text
claim: Repeatedly transforming inputs and measuring how stable their signal pattern stays gives features that separate source classes.
layout: 4 labeled stages, left-to-right, two parallel rows feeding a central stability panel
description: A wide four-stage flow diagram from left to right, with each stage titled in bold at the top. Stage 1 has a green box of human text sources (PG-19, CNN/DM, WikiText) above a blue box for watermarked LLMs. Stage 2 has two parallel rows. Each row has a gray paraphraser box that produces documents P1 through P8, followed by a binary sequence extraction box that outputs rows of red and green bars (D1 to D8). Both rows merge into a gray static-features box. Stage 3 is a large blue panel comparing AI and human bar sequences across D0 to D8. The AI bars are aligned with a vertical line and stay stable. The human bars are scrambled and linked by crossing dashed lines. Stage 4 has an XGBoost tree icon that outputs a teal Human-Written label or a blue AI-Generated label. The eye goes first to the red and green bar panel.
caption: End-to-end PSS pipeline. Human and AI-watermarked texts undergo up to eight paraphrasing rounds, with binary sequences extracted at each iteration (D0--D8). Watermarked text maintains stable patterns across iterations while human text shows random variation. An XGBoost classifier uses these stability features alongside static features for final classification.
abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) has intensified the demand for principled methods to distinguish human from machine-generated text. Watermarking provides a promising avenue, yet existing detectors exhibit sharp performance deterioration under multiple paraphrasing and when applied to shorter texts. We introduce Pattern Stability Score (PSS), a novel detection framework that leverages local statistical features and stability dynamics across paraphrased variants. Specifically, the proposed method combines global and local z-score features with higher-order statistics of run-length patterns, enriched by autocorrelation signals and stability scores computed over paraphrase depth. Numerical evaluations are performed on three benchmark datasets (PG-19, CNN/DailyMail, and WikiText) using multiple LLMs (Llama-3-8B, Qwen2-7B) and paraphrasers (Mistral-7B, Qwen2-7B, Gemma-7B), systematically stress-testing robustness under up to eight rounds of paraphrasing. Compared to prior z-score thresholding baselines and some state-of-the-art deep learning methods, our approach improves detection AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) by over 10-15 percentage points across different token lengths. Additionally, extensive cross-domain experiments demonstrate that a single universal classifier generalizes across different LLMs, paraphrasers, and text domains without retraining, maintaining above 87.8% AUC even when all components differ from training.
